mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the reaction of metals with water at room temperature?

options.A: All metals react rapidly with cold water.
options.B: Only the alkali metals react vigorously with cold water; other metals react, if at all, with steam or hot water.
options.C: No metal reacts with water under any condition.
options.D: Only noble metals such as gold and silver react with water.

mcqs.answer: Only the alkali metals react vigorously with cold water; other metals react, if at all, with steam or hot water.
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metals (e.g., Na, K) react vigorously with cold water, producing hydrogen gas and a hydroxide. Most other metals either do not react with cold water or require steam/hot water (e.g., Mg reacts with steam). Therefore option B accurately reflects the observed reactivity. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they either overgeneralize, deny all reactions, or attribute reactivity to noble metals that are actually unreactive with water.

mcqs.question: Metal X reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas. Which of the following metals will react most vigorously under the same conditions?
mcqs.explanation: The reactivity series (Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Cu > ... ) shows that magnesium is higher than zinc, iron, and copper. A metal higher in the series displaces hydrogen from acid more readily. Hence magnesium will react most vigorously, making option A correct. Copper, being low in the series, does not react appreciably with dilute HCl, so B is wrong. Iron and zinc react, but less vigorously than magnesium, so C and D are also incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which metal will displace hydrogen from an acid but will not react with cold water?
mcqs.explanation: Iron reacts with dilute acids (e.g., HCl) to produce hydrogen gas, but it does not react with cold water. Sodium reacts with both water and acids, calcium reacts slowly with hot water, and magnesium reacts with steam, not cold water. Therefore, option C correctly identifies a metal that shows hydrogen displacement with acids only.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions will NOT occur under standard conditions?
mcqs.explanation: In the reactivity series, copper is less reactive than silver; therefore copper cannot displace silver ions from AgNO₃. The other reactions involve a more reactive metal displacing a less reactive one (Zn > H, Fe > Cu, Al > H), so they are feasible. Hence option B is the only reaction that will not proceed.

mcqs.question: Which metal reacts with hot water to liberate hydrogen gas?
mcqs.explanation: Calcium reacts slowly with hot water, producing calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Sodium reacts with cold water, magnesium requires steam, and iron does not react with water under ordinary temperatures. Therefore option C correctly identifies the metal that reacts with hot water.

mcqs.question: Which of the following metals does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it does not displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Zinc, iron, and magnesium are all above hydrogen and will react, producing hydrogen gas. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: In a hydrogen displacement reaction, a metal reacts with an acid to produce hydrogen gas. Which equation best represents this type of reaction?
mcqs.explanation: A hydrogen displacement reaction involves a metal higher than hydrogen in the reactivity series reacting with an acid, forming a salt and releasing hydrogen gas. Option B captures this definition. Options A, C, and D describe different types of reactions (oxidation‑reduction, metal‑water reaction, and synthesis) and are not hydrogen displacement reactions.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: Which metal can be used to extract copper from its aqueous salt solution by displacement?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper ions from solutions such as CuSO₄, forming ZnSO₄ and metallic copper. Iron is also above copper but less commonly used for this purpose; magnesium and sodium are too reactive and would produce side reactions. Hence option A is the most appropriate choice.
